title: 纽约时报罗马分社社长：意大利是政治实验室，从贝卢斯科尼到梅洛尼
speaker: Jason Horowitz

segments.en: It's sort of a paradox because Italy doesn't really change much.
segments.zh: 这有点矛盾，因为意大利其实变化不大。

segments.en: And it's sort of structure, you know, the important things for Italians are that your inheritance laws are the same, your real estate isn't touched, right?
segments.zh: 它的结构，对意大利人来说重要的是继承法不变，房地产不动，对吧？

segments.en: They're very conservative. But that means that they will let anybody try anything, right?
segments.zh: 他们非常保守。但这意味着他们会让任何人尝试任何事，对吧？

segments.en: And so they're always looking for something new. And so if you look over the 25 years, you go from Berlusconi, who was, you know, the first mogul, media mogul politician.
segments.zh: 所以他们总在寻找新东西。看这25年，从贝卢斯科尼开始，他是第一个媒体大亨政治家。

segments.en: And then you go to left, you know, far, far left. You go to populists who were born on the internet, right?
segments.zh: 然后到左翼，极左。再到互联网上诞生的民粹主义者，对吧？

segments.en: All these sort of new things. And then now Georgia Maloney, who represents really the return of, you know, the post-fascists who were born after World War II, were kept out.
segments.zh: 所有这些新事物。现在乔治亚·梅洛尼，代表了二战后出生、曾被排除在外的后法西斯主义者的回归。

segments.en: And she's the first one who's been allowed back in, right? Now, and that is not saying that Georgia Maloney is a fascist or anything, but she comes out of that tradition.
segments.zh: 她是第一个被允许回归的人，对吧？这不是说梅洛尼是法西斯，但她出自那个传统。

segments.en: So you see a lot when you're in Italy, and it sort of teaches you what's coming elsewhere. That's my sort of main takeaway from it.
segments.zh: 在意大利你能看到很多，它教你其他地方会发生什么。这是我的主要收获。

segments.en: But you have the place changed, the politicians changed a lot. Please, maybe it's still the same. This is a wonderful cultural history of your time there.
segments.zh: 但地方变了，政客变了很多。也许本质还是一样。这是你那段时光的精彩文化史。

segments.en: It's also something that I think would strike a lot of envy and probably a hundred people I could get from this newsroom that you were able to move there after college.
segments.zh: 这也让很多人羡慕，新闻编辑室里大概有一百人羡慕你大学毕业后能搬去那里。

segments.en: The dollar was strong that buffeted all this, but you were able to make a go of it in the way that you did.
segments.zh: 美元强劲缓冲了这一切，但你以你的方式成功了。

segments.en: And you know, you end up at the New York Times on the heels of that. What do you say to young journalists today who look at your career and say, that's it, I'd love to be able to do that?
segments.zh: 你随后进了纽约时报。你对今天看着你职业生涯说“我也想那样”的年轻记者说什么？

segments.en: Yeah, I mean, yeah, okay, so obviously it wasn't easy. It wasn't a straight shot.
segments.zh: 是的，显然不容易。不是一帆风顺。

segments.en: No, it was not. In the past have totally changed, but I, the one thing I feel very strongly about in journalism is to go right.
segments.zh: 不，不是。过去完全变了，但我对新闻业感受强烈的一点是：去现场。

segments.en: So whether it be a story, right, if you have the opportunity to go to do it, do it right. And there's nothing, there's nothing that comes close to being on the ground.
segments.zh: 所以无论是报道，如果有机会去，就去做。没有什么比得上亲临现场。
